blocks.text: Witness statement of DR ASTHA SONI (read)
My Lord, may I hand up a copy of a statement from a witness, Dr Soni.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Then, members of the jury, I will read the relevant parts of this statement to you. You may recall mention of Dr Soni on Friday and her clinical notes are on the chronology, obviously, and they begin at tile 321.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: In the witness statement I'm about to read she makes reference to some of the notes that she created, so we'll read the statement and refer to the original clinical notes where relevant.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Dr Soni made a statement on 26 October 2018. She sets out her experience and qualifications and at our page 45, my Lord, she says at paragraph 18 of her statement, under the heading "Lucy Letby":
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I vaguely recall working with Lucy Letby whilst I was at the Countess of Chester Hospital between September 2015 and March 2016. I recall that Lucy Letby worked within the neonatal unit and as a neonatal nurse.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: I believe she would always ask for help if she was concerned."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: So having dealt with that and other general matters she says:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I worked at the Countess of Chester Hospital as an ST8 in paediatrics between September 2015 and March 2016."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: So that would be as a registrar?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Indeed, as a senior registrar.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: She then speaks of [Baby H], date of birth 22 September 2015, and confirms that she, Dr Soni, had been provided access to [Baby H]'s notes.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: She reiterates that [Baby H] was born at 34 plus 4 weeks' gestation. At our page 47, paragraph 28, my Lord, she says:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I had no involvement until 24 September 2015 and I have recorded an entry in the notes at 15.30 hours."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: That's in a different part of the note. I'll go back to that in due course. She says:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I have recorded that Dr Gibbs spoke to [Baby H]'s parents because they were upset. They felt that they were not informed about the events that had taken place earlier that morning. Dr Gibbs apologised for this, but explained that stabilising [Baby H] was the priority for the medical team. The parents will be informed at the earliest opportunity from now on."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: And you'll remember Dr Gibbs making reference to this on Friday, I'm sure, members of the jury.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Her note within the clinical records says:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "15.30. 24 September 15. Parents spoken to by Dr John Gibbs. Parents upset as they feel they were not informed about this morning's events in time. Dr Gibbs apologised but explained that [Baby H] was fine at 7 am and had sudden deterioration. Medical and nursing team's first priority was to stabilise [Baby H]. Parents were informed at the earliest opportunity but we still apologised for the delay if the parents feel that there was one."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Moving on -- and this is the entry behind tile 321:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "On 26 September 2015 I saw her on my ward round.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: There is an entry from me at 09.15 hours. My entry in the medical records..."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: And if you put the actual records up, I'm grateful, Mr Murphy, it has the date and the time and the following detail:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "34.4, day 5. 35.2. Weight 2.530 kilograms.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Problems: IDM, RDS, tension pneumothorax. Chest drain times 3. Presumed sepsis."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Then you can see the entries alongside a V in a circle for ventilation:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "SIMV 22/5. FiO2 6%. Sats greater than 95%. Rate [heart rate] 50 beats per minute.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Chest drains times 3. Several needle thoracocenteses in last 48 hours. CVS: HR 140 to 149 minutes (sic). BP [blood pressure] mean 38 to 44."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: The fluids are stated there. Other data -- I'm not sure it all merits reading out, but I will if anyone specifically asks me to:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Had a blood transfusion last night. Sepsis. On benpen day 5 [a reference to antibiotics there]. CRP 6 yesterday. On examination settled. CVS 1/11/0. Chest: good chest wall movement, good air entry bilaterally."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: She draws the familiar image of the chest that we've seen in many a clinical note previously. On this drawing has included three chest drains. And the note says:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Not seen swinging or bubbling."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: And you heard on Friday what a swinging or a bubbling chest drain means:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Latest chest X-ray shows lungs re-expanded. Baby's abdomen was soft and not distended."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: If we can scroll down a little more, Mr Murphy:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Access: one long line. Cannula in the left hand.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Area of pale ? ischaemic area."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: And then the plan was to:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Continue ventilation, wean pressures slowly if gasses allow. To continue the fluids. To add CRP on this morning's blood test regime."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: I assume that means:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Discuss with Arrowe Park or Liverpool Women's Hospital about the possibility of a transfer. Discuss with Dr Saladi about the possibility of taking the first drain out. Re-cannulate and inform if concerns."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: So returning to the witness statement it says:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "In summary [Baby H] was 5 days old and had three chest drains in situ at this point. She was on a ventilator.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: I have summarised the relevant points from the previous night. At that stage she was relatively stable.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: I noted that her left hand, which had her cannula in place, was pale, which is possibly due to ischaemia. My plan was to wean her ventilation slowly, as she tolerates, to continue the same fluids, and to review the fluid balance every 12 hours.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I added an additional blood investigation of CRP.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: I was also to discuss with Arrowe Park/Liverpool Women's Hospital regarding her management, update and whether transfer was available. I was also to discuss with Dr Saladi, the consultant, if we should take the first chest drain out."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: There's a further entry made by me at 11.45.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: I think that would be behind tile 341, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: This is a record of a communication with Arrowe Park, effectively:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I discussed [Baby H]'s case with Dr Rath at Arrowe Park Hospital. My note reads as follows:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "'Discussed with Dr Rath, consultant neonatologist, Arrowe Park. Explained [Baby H]'s clinical condition, if they want her to be transferred over. They wouldn't at present as difficult to transfer with drains and stable (sic) but advised to (1) clamp the drain, to repeat the chest X-ray in 6 hours, and if no reaccumulation then take that drain out.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "'(2) Possible cause for cardiac arrest could be that a drain is too close to heart and touching pericardium. Can [the note says 'put' but the doctor thinks she meant to write 'pull'] drain out if too far in. Shouldn't be close to midline.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "'(3) To get access for invasive blood pressure monitoring. To have an arterial line.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "'(4) To update him [that is Dr Rath] this evening or earlier if deterioration or things change. Parents updated about the plan.'"
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: In summary the doctor says:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I asked them whether they would like us to transfer [Baby H] over to Arrowe Park and they said they would not advise that as
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: she was unstable and had three drains in situ but gave me advice about further management."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: That advice is as per the note and unless I'm requested to do so, I don't read it out again.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: The next and final note is an entry made at 20.20 hours, which, Mr Murphy, should be behind tile 393.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: It's a brief note that says:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Chest drain number 1 taken out as chest X-ray showed no accumulation."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: The witness statement says:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "The chest drain was removed as there was shown to be no accumulation.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "According to the medical records [Baby H] had another deterioration overnight. I was not involved at that stage. She was transferred to Arrowe Park Hospital that night. I had no further involvement in the care of [Baby H]."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: So that's Dr Soni's contribution.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: My Lord, I've been passed information to the effect that we can now link to Australia.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: MS SHELLEY TOMLINS (recalled)
Examination-in-chief by MR DRIVER
Good morning, Ms Tomlins. Can you see and hear us clearly?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I can.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: I'm grateful. Could you state your full name for the record, please?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Shelley Anne Tomlins.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: I think you anticipate that we're going to ask you questions today about the events on the night shift of 26 September 2015; were you aware of that?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: I'm grateful. Have you had the opportunity to refresh your memory from a witness statement that you made about your involvement with baby [Baby H] during that shift?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. I read it around 10 days ago because I thought I was due in court on the 13th, so I haven't read it since then, but I'm somewhat refreshed.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: I'm grateful. I'm going to take you to the nursing notes that you made during that shift and we'll use that as the basis -- as a structure to your evidence. Do you understand?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Mr Murphy, could we go to tile 392, please, and the notes that lie behind it.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It's the large entry at the right side of the page, thank you.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Ms Tomlins, can you confirm that you can still hear me?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I can.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. Could you confirm that you can see on screen a section of nursing notes that bears your initials and is timed as being created at 22.53 hours on 26 September 2015?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. It's slightly fuzzy -- oh, that's better, thanks.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Good, I'm grateful. So we know that you were working a night shift on this day. Can you confirm that you were the designated nurse for [Baby H]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I was.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: As you've told us previously was your practice at the start of the shift, would you have checked the baby's fluids, medical infusions, the apparatus, the endotracheal tube, the ventilator settings and would you have checked the CPR equipment?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I would have checked all of it.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. Your note tells us, and could you confirm, that when you took over the care of [Baby H] she was already ventilated with a size 3.5 tube, which was initially 8 centimetres at the lip, but at some point changed to a position at 7.5 centimetres?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I can confirm that.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. Your note tells us that good air entry was heard bilaterally. Was that a piece of monitoring that you undertook or was that information provided to you by your predecessor?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Probably both. So we would check with a stethoscope every hour for air entry ourselves.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. And can you confirm that when she came into your care that she was stable on the ventilator and that she had already three chest drains inserted into the left side of her body?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I can confirm that.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: And of the chest drains, two were the flutter variety and the third was a conventional chest drain?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: One of which had been removed, you confirmed, did you, at 20.15 hours, so during your shift, the early part of your shift, Dr Soni removed a chest drain?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, at 8.15.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: I'm grateful. Could you tell us how that went from your perspective?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Um... Yes, I've written that she tolerated it well, so that probably means she was quite stable whilst we were doing it.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. And you also noted that some morphine, a morphine bolus, had been administered prior to this intervention. Would that simply have been for pain relief for the baby?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, it would have.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Let's now move on, please, to the event that occurred at around 20.30 hours, half past 8, during your night shift. Can you, with the assistance of the nursing notes to refresh your memory, tell us what you recall happening with [Baby H] at this time?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. I can't actually remember it, but from my notes I've written that she had a profound desaturation and brady, so her oxygen sats dropped and heart rate did as well and that we can no longer hear air going into the lungs via the ETT, so we had to remove it and call the doctors.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. So there's no audible evidence of air entering the chest and did you at this point also check the capnograph device?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, we did, and that was negative, so it wasn't detecting any carbon dioxide, so that confirmed that the ETT was blocked or dislodged.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. So a potential emergency situation. The doctors were crash called and was the tube removed?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, it was.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: What did you find at this point in time?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Um... Sorry, I'm not sure what you mean by the question. Do you mean how she was at that point in time or...?
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Yes. Upon the removal of the ET tube, did that have the desired effect?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. So I've written that she bagged up well, so we were able to Neopuff her with a jaw thrust. "Bagging up well" means that their saturations improve when we do that, so she responded well to that.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. Did you -- and again please refresh your memory from this note -- examine the tube itself?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Um... I'm just going to have a quick read.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Of course.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: (Pause)
I'm not sure. I haven't written that I have, so I can't remember. Usually, we would look at it to see whether it was blocked, but I haven't actually written what we could see, sorry.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: That's okay. I'm referring to the part of the note that begins:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "Copious secretions obtained via ETT and orally, bloodstained."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Ah. One moment. Yes, it's hard to know whether that means from the first ETT that we had to remove or whether it's from the new one. I think from the new one but it's hard to be completely sure.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. If you're uncertain then don't hesitate to say so.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Okay, thanks.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: So it would seem that Dr Neame responded to the crash call; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: And it was him, Dr Neame, who introduced a new ETT?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, it was him, yes.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: So you leave open the possibility that the copious secretions that you record as being obtained may have been obtained from the original ET tube in place when you took over care or obtained from that inserted by Dr Neame at around 8.30; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. I think judging by where I've written that in the kind of sequence of events in the notes, I think it does mean the new one. But yeah, hard to be -- I think that's what it means.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: The next entry in the nursing notes seems to be a plan of action; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "For frequent suction overnight, one to two-hourly."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. Just because of the amount of secretions, yes.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: So that's a reference to suction from the ET tube; yes?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I think probably ETT and orally, but in particular the ETT to stop it blocking with all the secretions.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. Thereafter, there is reference to the fluid regime and then, finally, a report of [Baby H]'s general condition; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. So at this stage, that event having occurred, Dr Neame having addressed the issue, are you able to remember how [Baby H] was, what sort of condition she was in at this point in time?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I can't remember off the top of my head, no, unfortunately.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Very well. Looking down the page, your next entry, made a little later, but a record of a further event at 21.45 hours; do you see that?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I think it needs to be scrolled down so I can see, sorry.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: You're probably right. You are absolutely right.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Thanks.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: There we go, thank you. Do you see that brief note made at 23.09 and a reference to events at 21.45?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Can you tell us what happened at this point in time, please?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. So her oxygen saturation levels dropped to 40%, but this time we could still hear air entry and we could detect carbon dioxide on the capnograph, so the tube was in the right position. So she needed to be suctioned and they were thick and bloodstained, the secretions.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Right. Is that an unusual discovery, thick bloodstained secretions, in circumstances such as those that you were faced with this evening?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Well, you wouldn't normally see bloodstains on an average day, but seeing as she'd just been re-intubated it's quite normal to see a little bit of blood after that because sometimes that procedure can cause a little bit of throat trauma. So it's not unusual in that it was just after being intubated.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. At the very bottom of this page there is a further note made later in the morning, but a note of events that took place at 00.55 hours. Do you see the single line at the bottom of the page?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I can see that.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: So we'll consider this. It says:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "Profound desaturation to 40% despite equal bilateral air entry."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: We'll just pause at that part of that sentence for a moment.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Profound desaturation to 40%; 40% of what?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Oxygen saturation of the blood down to 40%.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: You noted that that happened, and your words, "despite equal bilateral air entry". Why have you phrased it in that way?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I can't remember exactly, but I think because even though air was going into both lungs, she still desaturated to 40%, so I think that's why I've used the word "despite".
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. If you could just bear with us for a moment, I'll ask Mr Murphy, please, to take us to tile 442 and we'll see the remainder of this note. There we are.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Is that legible for you, Ms Tomlins?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: So this is a continuation of the same sentence, which began:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "Profound desaturations to 40% despite equal bilateral air entry and positive capnography."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So does that flow from there, that you were satisfied that air was going in and carbon dioxide was coming out at this point?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, it does.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: And did you undertake that investigation, as it were, to try and ascertain the cause of the profound desaturation?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, we would have wanted to check whether the tube was still in the right place or whether it had blocked from secretions.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. So did you check it, the tube, for secretions?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, and there weren't any, judging by what I've written.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: So whatever was happening here wasn't being caused by a blocked ET tube?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No, it wasn't.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: What happened next?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: She went bradycardic at 01.07, so her heart rate dropped and she required chest compressions and adrenaline at 01.08.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: So CPR, emergency CPR, was applied to the baby; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: We'll hear from the medics involved in that in due course, but did you note in the records that a saline bolus was given to the baby during this, in addition to adrenaline?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I did, yes.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: And was the cold light test undertaken to try to determine whether or not there'd been a further pneumothorax?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, and there hadn't been.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. A chest X-ray was ordered to take a more thorough examination for potential pneumothorax. So having nursed [Baby H] during this time, can you offer any explanation as to why this desaturation occurred?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No, I can't.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Looking a little further down your nursing note, we can see that there was a further event at 03.30 hours.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I can see that.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Another, your phrase, profound desaturation, this time —
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: -- to the 60s. Is that another reference to the oxygen levels?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, it's 60-something per cent, that would have been.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: On this occasion she required Neopuffing; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, she did, yes.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: You note that there was "No known cause for desat".
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Can we infer from that that you checked for what might be the predictable causes?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, so it said I can still hear bilateral air entry and capnography was still positive, so we checked.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Yes. Orally, it would seem there were copious amounts of secretions, pink-tinged secretions; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: That's right, yes.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Could you just explain to the jury, it might be obvious, these were "yielded orally". What's the actual method, what would you have done with the baby at that point to yield those secretions?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I would have attached a suction catheter, like a long tube, to the suction machine and I would have opened her mouth and suctioned kind of, you know, under the tongue and off -sometimes into the back of the throat a little bit as well, just got rid of whatever was in there.
blocks.speaker: TOMLINS

blocks.text: Thank you. Does it follow from your next entry that you would have repeated a similar check or intervention with the ET tube?

blocks.text: "We discussed over the phone to tease out the causes of the cardiac arrest that this baby had suffered and we discussed the main causes of cardiac arrest.

blocks.text: Could it be due to a blocked endotracheal tube, chest drain related mechanical position (drain end too far in and irritating the heart muscle)? If there was an accumulation of air which
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: could have caused this baby to have cardiac arrest as it is not usual for a baby to have multiple cardiac arrests.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "We discussed the above causes and the registrar stated they had looked at these causes and they were not able to ascertain a reason for the arrests.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Following this discussion, I advised the local team to get an electrocardiogram (ECG). I also advised the local team to clamp the old chest drain which had been there for more than 2 days and had been non-functional, to do a repeat chest X-ray after clamping and look for any re-accumulation of air and, if none, was identified, to remove the chest drain. To continue to wean off the ventilation and plan for extubation provided baby was stable and the gases were good.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I also asked the registrar to discuss my advice with the oncall consultant, liaise with myself if there were any changes in the clinical condition of the baby and for further clarity in terms of management was needed."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: That doesn't quite make sense but that's what it reads:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "At that point in time the baby was stable, on minimal ventilation, was clearly getting better, and the local team who had managed the baby for the 48 hours were confident to continue looking after the baby.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: I did not feel that transferring the baby to a level 3 unit to de-escalate intensive management would be the right decision in the baby's or family's interest.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: It would make more sense for the local team to continue managing the baby with an attempt to wean and extubate locally in the next 24 hours with guidance and support from us and to contact us if they encountered any difficulties.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Unexpectedly, I got a call from the on-call paediatric consultant at Chester in the early morning hours of 27 September 2015..."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: It's Dr Saladi's note that we've just looked at, members of the jury:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "... saying that the baby had suffered another unexplained cardiac arrest while being on the ventilator. Following that, I decided to mobilise the baby to the nearest level 3 neonatal unit, which was Arrowe Park Hospital, and asked the consultant to contact the transport team for an uplift and transfer.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "This was my service week in the neonatal unit at Arrowe Park Hospital. I was subsequently involved in the care of this baby in the neonatal unit over the next 2 days until discharge back to Chester. blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "In the unit the baby's management was quickly de-intensified. Chest drains were removed. Ventilation was weaned and she was extubated. blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "We carried out an echocardiogram, which showed a structurally normal heart with mildly raised pulmonary pressure (normal for
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: this age in babies). An ECG was planned but did not happen due to difficulty in sticking the ECG lead patches on the chest due to the chest being covered with chest drains and Tegaderms. blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "The notes show that [Baby H] arrived at Arrowe Park at 06.50 hours on 27 September. However, it may have been a little earlier as the note may have been written retrospectively."

blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: He then refers to his notes and if Mr Murphy could take us to the next tile, please. This is a note made by Dr Babarao, as we'll see in a moment. So two pages, beginning with the time and date. A phone call from a colleague of his, who he will refer to in a moment when I return to his statement.

blocks.text: He says:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "From my notes I have written that the baby is a 34 weeks' gestation baby, day 5 of life. Was born after induction of labour. It looked like the mother had type 1 diabetes mellitus and the baby was born in a fair condition at birth. Needed CPAP,
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: which is a form of respiratory support, for the first 2 days, and then the baby started deteriorating on 24 September, which was 2 days later.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "The baby had a tension pneumothorax on the left side, meaning there was air leak into the chest cavity on the left side outside the lung, which needed a chest drain insertion. blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: If we could then go, please, Mr Murphy, to tile 503 and we'll see what lies behind that.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I have also written in my notes on 26 September 2015 that in the early hours, which was 24 hours' time from referral, the baby had an episode of collapse, which means that there was a prolonged bradycardia. blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: That's why I have written 'ET change' and the baby needed 20 minutes of cardiopulmonary resuscitation and I have written that the baby became stable after that, was stable for 24 hours, then had a blocked endotracheal tube later that evening, which had to be changed again, so on the same night, I think the episode they are talking about, at 01.00 hours the baby had a desaturation whereby the oxygen levels reduced and bradycardia, low heart rate, and the endotracheal tube was changed again. blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: So at the time they thought about whether the baby had any cardiac problem or whether there were any neurological problems that was making the baby behave like this.

blocks.text: "Further on they said at the point of referral the baby was stable, on the ventilator, and SIMV is a mode of ventilation. The ventilator settings are not hugely significant. blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I have written that the blood pressure was acceptable, which was 33 cuff blood pressure, and urine output, which was 5ml per kilogram per hour, which was again good. We did not have a potassium sample, which is K+, which I have written, but it was previously normal.

blocks.text: "I have also written there were no risk factors for infection and the CRP, which is an infection marker, was 6, which is not really high. The baby was cultured again, meaning blood cultures were sent after the deterioration, and I have written the blood sugars remained stable.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I have written that the baby had a long line sited in the right arm and the tip was in the subclavian vein, which is an acceptable position. blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I asked whether they had done a cranial ultrasound scan and they said it was normal and the baby did not have any clinical seizure-like activity, meaning there were no fits. I was just ruling out whether there was any cardiac or neurological issues. I have written:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "'I have given a plan to them to check calcium, magnesium and potassium levels and suggested to them to change the second line antibiotics.'

blocks.text: "Meaning change the antibiotic to a higher coverage. I suggested to them to put a second cannula, like a venous line, and then I said to try an arterial line, meaning -- which is like another line going into the artery so we can monitor blood pressure properly."

blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: We can see here the measurements taken of [Baby H] at 045 (sic), at which point in time she had been transferred to the transport incubator. Both chest drains connected to a flutter valve each. There was no swinging, flutter or draining noted from either drain.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: The last sentence of that paragraph, I've not read it all, says:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Minimal mucky [I think that says, maybe mucousy possibly] aspirate from the NGT."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: If we scroll down to the bottom of these notes, please. Pausing there, we can see the top line:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Cuff BP [blood pressure] satisfactory."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: So these are the measurements taken of the baby as she's being placed in the transport vehicle and then en route from Chester to Arrowe Park, which event we can see occurred at 05.30, despatched (inaudible) Chester.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: At 05.45, [Baby H] was settled, and the observations were within the normal limits, satisfactory. Again no swinging or fluttering from the drains.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: At 06.00 hours it is recorded that the transport team and [Baby H] arrived at Arrowe Park. The handover was given to staff within Arrowe Park. Again, reading below there:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "BP and [I think that says 'heart'] satisfactory.

blocks.text: Infusions satisfactory."

blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: I can't read the next word, but then "very good", I think it says. The ventilation rate was reduced to a level of 40 beats per minute and the baby was transferred to Arrowe Park equipment, that is to say taken off the transport equipment and handed over, effectively, into the care of Arrowe Park.

blocks.text: If we could go to tile 504, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Returning to Dr Babarao's statement, he states:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "At 5.30 on 27 September I have written a retrospective note at Chester or I would have written this en route from Chester to Arrowe Park after I have stabilised and moved the baby on to the transport incubator.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I have recalled things that I have done at Chester.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: I have written from the ventilation perspective the baby was stable. The oxygen requirement was less than 30%, which is not worrying at all, and the chest X-ray I reviewed revealed no pneumothorax, meaning no air leak, and the blood gases were good. Fluids are retained at 150ml per kilogram per day on TPN, but we changed to 10% glucose because during transfer we cannot take parenteral nutrition, so we stop it and change to a plain 10% glucose infusion.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Blood pressures were fine at 38 to 42 cuff, which was good for that gestation. The capillary refill time was less than 2 seconds, which is also normal. Heart rate was 130, which was normal. Blood sugars were stable. No bradycardia, meaning no heart rate drop.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: The base deficit, which is BE, were written at minus 2, which is normal. For urine output, I put a tick, which means there was good urine output, which means it's reassuring. Medications are 'Second line antibiotics commenced'..."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: And he states the particular antibiotics:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "... which was per protocol at Chester. Also, I have written that the CRP had gone up to 49, which is high, and morphine was being administered at 40 micrograms per kilogram per hour, which is a little higher than the usual sedation dose for the baby.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Temperature at 36.3 is slightly low for a baby. I have written 'Full blood count within normal limits'.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Potassium was normal, 3.7. The platelet count was 311, which is again normal. Haemoglobin 107, which is sort of normal for this age. I have written 'Intravenous long line right upper limb'. I have seen the X-ray. It was subclavian, in position on X-ray, which is not the best position but acceptable.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I have written 'positional', which means the long line worked better when the upper limb was kept in certain position, which is again not unusual.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "The transport team included myself and Sandra Osaka(?). We went to Chester to transfer this baby to Arrowe Park, transfer date 27 September.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "The first gas was noted at 05.10, which means I was at Chester Hospital and the baby was on the transport ventilator, so that means I was ready to move from Chester to Arrowe Park.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "At 05.55 is the time I arrived at Arrowe Park.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Upon arrival at Arrowe Park a further blood gas was done. Both these gases were very good so I had no concerns. The transfer to Arrowe Park was uneventful.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: There were no adverse effects, no issues, no intervention. The care was carried over to the medical and nursing team at Arrowe Park."
